issues.failure_explanation: The right-hand side |sup f| is not a norm: for any f in P_t the polynomial g=f-sup f has sup g=0, so the inequality forces exact equality c∫_γ g=∫g; applying this to f and −f gives (cℓ−1)sup f=(cℓ−1)inf f for all f, hence cℓ=1 and c∫_γ f=∫f exactly. As literally written every (ε,c)-approximate t-design curve is an exact t-design curve, making the approximate setting vacuous. The same misuse appears in the L^p display and in (eq:submfld), and Remark rmk:changec's equality step also depends on the intended norm sup|f|.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace |sup_{S^d} f| by ‖f‖_∞=sup_{S^d}|f| throughout (Definition def:design, Lemma lem:overlap, Remark rmk:changec, Subsection sub:norm, eq:submfld) and correct the L^p display to (∫|f|^p dσ)^{1/p}.
issues.overall_effect: All statements about (ε,c)-approximate designs are ill-posed as literally defined; they only make sense with ‖f‖_∞=sup|f|.
issues.title: Approximate-design definition uses |sup f| instead of sup|f|, which forces exactness
issues.why_classification: The intended norm is clear and the substitution is uniform and local; all arguments go through unchanged with the correct norm.

issues.failure_explanation: The lift (eq:explicitweight3) divides by sqrt(1+α_3(r)) and Theorem thm:S3stitch requires α_R=α_3≠−1. One has α_3=−1 exactly when α_1=0 and sin(πk/t+θ_1(0))=−1 for some k∈{0,…,2t−1}, i.e. θ_1(0)=−π/2+2mπ−kπ/t. The stated exclusion θ_1(0)≠mπ−2nπ/t is a different set: e.g. t=4, θ_1≡−3π/4 satisfies the hypothesis, yet on the segment k=1 one gets sin(π/4−3π/4)=−1, so α_3=−1 and the formula has a 0/0 with a phase jump (the lifted curve is discontinuous), so the theorem's conclusion for that θ_1 fails.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the hypothesis by θ_1(0)≠−π/2+2mπ−kπ/t for all m∈Z, k∈{0,…,2t−1} (equivalently α_3≠−1 along the curve).
issues.overall_effect: The d=3 explicit part of Theorem thm:weight is false for some θ_1 allowed by its hypothesis.
issues.title: Stated condition on θ_1(0) does not guarantee well-definedness of the S^3 formula
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the hypothesis restores the statement; no argument changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: w_\Bbb R(s)=(-1)^i(2(s-\Lambda_{i-1})-1), \quad w_{\Bbb R^d}(s)=\sqrt{1-w_\Bbb R(s)^2}M(w_\Bbb R(s))x_i

issues.failure_explanation: The last equality asserts that (1/2)∫_{-1}^1 (normalized slice average of f at height s) ds equals ∫_{S^d} f dσ. This is Archimedes' hat-box property, valid only for d=2; for d≥3 the pushforward of σ to the height coordinate has density ∝(1−s²)^{(d−2)/2}, not uniform. Concretely, for d=3 and f=ω_1²: ∫_0^1 f(w_{X,M}(s))ds=(1/2)∫_{-1}^1 u² du=1/3, while ∫_{S^3}ω_1² dσ=1/4, for every X and M. Hence w_{X,M} is not a weighted t-design curve for any t≥2 when d≥3, and Theorem thm:weightconst is false as stated. (Also, the displayed w_R omits division by λ(x_i), needed for the segment to span [−1,1]; and the proof needs positive weights.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reparametrize the height: replace the linear w_R on each segment by the quantile function of the marginal density c_d(1−u²)^{(d−2)/2} du on [−1,1] (scaled by λ(x_i)); then the change of variables in the proof yields the correct sphere measure, the image, length π|X| and singular set are unchanged, and thm:weight/thm:weightstrength follow as before.
issues.overall_effect: The general-d existence claims of Theorem thm:weight (d≥4), Theorem thm:weightstrength, the simplex/cross-polytope remarks and Figure Weightex2 rely on this construction and are unsupported; the explicit d=2 formula and the d=3 formula via thm:S3stitch are unaffected.
issues.title: Construction w_{X,M} is not a weighted t-design curve for d≥3 (wrong height distribution)
issues.why_classification: The theorem is false as written for all d≥3 and the construction itself must be changed, but a contained reparametrization restores every conclusion and rate without new global architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
there exists a smooth $(\varepsilon+2\delta c,c)$-approximate
$t$-design curve $\widetilde\gamma$ on $S^d$ of length $\ell(\widetilde\gamma)=\ell(\gamma)+\delta$. If $d\neq2$, we may take $\widetilde\gamma$ to be simple.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof removes a portion of γ of length δ/2 and replaces it with a smooth portion of length δ/2, giving ℓ(γ̃)=ℓ(γ), not ℓ(γ)+δ; Lemma lem:overlap then yields error ε+δc, not ε+2δc as claimed. The proof also applies lem:overlap with L=γ([0,1]) without ensuring γ is simple (otherwise ∫_L f ds≠∫_γ f and |L|≠ℓ(γ)), and the simplicity claim 'if d≠2' is false for d=1 (a curve winding twice around S^1 cannot be made simple).

failure_location.quote: We may then smooth $\gamma$ to any curve $\widetilde\gamma$ which coincides with $\gamma$ on $[0,1]\setminus S$ and satisfies $\ell(\widetilde\gamma|_{S})=\delta/2$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Take the smoothing pieces of total length 3δ/2 (so ℓ(γ̃)=ℓ(γ)+δ and lem:overlap gives ε+2δc), state the lemma for simple γ or handle multiplicities, and restrict the simplicity claim to d≥3.
issues.overall_effect: The lemma's stated quantitative guarantee is not what the proof gives; uses in the introduction (smooth versions of thm:const/thm:main) rest on it.
issues.title: Proof of Lemma lem:smooth does not produce the stated length/error
issues.why_classification: Routine local adjustments to the construction and hypotheses recover the stated statement.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then, we see that any $(\varepsilon,c,||\cdot||_2)$-approximate $t$-design curve is a $(C_t\varepsilon,c,||\cdot||_1)$-approximate $t$-design curve.
so we may take $C_t:=1$ to prove Remark \ref{rmk:p}.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper's own lemma passes from ‖·‖_2-approximate to ‖·‖_1-approximate when ‖·‖_2≤C_t‖·‖_1. Taking ‖·‖_2=‖·‖_p and ‖·‖_1=‖·‖_∞ with ‖f‖_p≤‖f‖_∞ shows L^p-approximate ⇒ L^∞-approximate, the opposite of the Remark. Passing from an L^∞ bound to an L^p bound requires ‖f‖_∞≤C‖f‖_p (Nikolskii), whose constant grows like t^{d/p}. The Remark is false: for p=1 take f≥0 a bump polynomial supported away from an ε-approximate cycle γ with ε<1; then |(1/ℓ)∫_γ f−∫f|=‖f‖_1>ε‖f‖_1.

failure_location.quote: any $\varepsilon$-approximate $t$-design cycle on $S^d$ is a ($\varepsilon,||\cdot||_p$)-approximate $t$-design cycle on $S^d$ for all $p\in\Bbb N$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Invoke a Nikolskii inequality ‖f‖_∞≤C t^{d/p}‖f‖_p on P_t(S^d) to obtain (C t^{d/p}ε_t,‖·‖_p)-approximation, and restrict the MZ-family claim to exponents where t^{d/p}ε_t stays bounded (p>d for ε_t≍1/t), or withdraw the L^p claims.
issues.overall_effect: Remark rmk:p, Remark rmk:MZ (Marcinkiewicz–Zygmund family for all even q with the same ε_t) and the corresponding introduction paragraph are unsupported/false.
issues.title: L^p-approximate design claim uses the norm inequality in the wrong direction
issues.why_classification: A genuinely different (Nikolskii) argument is needed and the result survives only in a materially weakened form (larger constants, restricted p), while the main theorems are unaffected.

issues.failure_explanation: On the fiber over a non-root y there are n_y+1 special points: the arrival point g_{z_y}(1) (angle 0) and n_y departure points at angles 2πj/n_y+δ_{d_{y,j}}. For j=n_y the angle is 2π+δ_{d_{y,n_y}}≡δ_{d_{y,n_y}}, and δ_{d_{y,n_y}}∈[0,2π/N_Y−δ̃) may be smaller than δ̃ (e.g. 0), so the gap arc of D_{d_{y,n_y}} overlaps the arrival arc of D_y. The displayed inequality only checks consecutive j−1,j and never the wrap-around, so the claimed pairwise disjointness (and hence the length accounting |∪D_y|=δ) is not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Space the n_y+1 special points on the fiber by using angles 2πj/(n_y+1) (root: 2πj/n_{y_0}); since n_y+1≤N_Y for non-root y, the same inequality then covers all consecutive gaps including the wrap-around.
issues.overall_effect: As written the construction may fail to be a simple cycle with the stated removed length; thm:const and thm:main rely on the lemma.
issues.title: Fiber gap arcs D_y can overlap: wrap-around case not covered by the spacing argument
issues.why_classification: A one-parameter change in the construction fixes the gap and all lengths/conclusions are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Formula (eq:MDelta) is valid only in geodesic normal coordinates at p. The proof asserts that the pullbacks Π^*x_i^C of normal coordinates on CP^n extend to normal coordinates on S^{2n+1}. This is false: along the sphere geodesic cos(s)ω+sin(s)(h+a·iω) one has d_{CP^n}(w,Π(·))=arcsin(|h|sin s)≠s|h|, so Σ_{i≤2n}(Π^*x_i^C)² is not the squared normal-coordinate radius. Hence the computation Δ(Π^*g)=Δ^C g is not justified as written (although the identity is true by the Riemannian-submersion/totally-geodesic-fiber property).

failure_location.quote: Setting $x_i:=\Pi^*x_i^{\Bbb C}$, we may then consider geodesic normal coordinates $\{x_i:S^{2n+1}\to\Bbb R\}_{i=1}^{2n+1}$ on $S^{2n+1}$ in a neighborhood $U$ of $\omega$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the coordinate argument by the standard fact that for the Riemannian submersion Π with totally geodesic fibers, Δ_{S^{2n+1}}Π^*=Π^*Δ_{CP^n} on functions constant on fibers (or cite the known spectrum of CP^n).
issues.overall_effect: The 'full proof for completeness' of P_t=R_t contains an invalid step; the lemma's conclusion remains true.
issues.title: Pulled-back coordinates are not geodesic normal coordinates on S^{2n+1}
issues.why_classification: The conclusion is standard and true; only a citation or short replacement argument is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: considering the covering radius $\rho_t$ of $Y_t$, we can see that $W_t\leq (|Y_t|-1)\rho_t/4$

issues.failure_explanation: D_t as defined is the maximal nearest-neighbour distance, not the covering radius sup_x inf_y d(x,y) that the cited Breger–Ehler–Gräf result bounds. The stated D_t≍1/t is false in general: the union of a design Y_t with a slightly rotated copy is again an R_t-design with D_t arbitrarily small, so no lower bound ≳1/t holds. The proof of thm:main then invokes this proposition for 'the covering radius ρ_t', a quantity the proposition never mentions.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the proposition as: the covering radius ρ_t of an R_t-design sequence satisfies ρ_t≲1/t (as in the cited theorem), and use only that in thm:main.
issues.overall_effect: The bound W_t≲t^{2n−1} in the proof of thm:main (and hence ε_t≲1/t, and thm:even) is not supported by the proposition as stated.
issues.title: Proposition pro:covrad states separation, not covering radius, and claims a false two-sided asymptotic
issues.why_classification: A correct restatement of the cited result is a local fix that fully supports the downstream use.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem claims ε_t≍1/t but the proof only derives the upper bound W_t≲t^{2n−1}, hence ε_t=W_t/(π|Y_t|)≲1/t; no lower bound W_t≳t^{2n−1} is argued (it needs, e.g., that the connected set Π(Γ) must be ρ_t-dense so its length is ≳ρ_t^{1−2n}). Moreover the asserted inequality W_t≤(|Y_t|−1)ρ_t/4 is unsupported and its constant is wrong: W_t is twice the MST weight and MST edges are only bounded by 2ρ_t via a bottleneck argument, giving W_t≤4(|Y_t|−1)ρ_t; a two-point set at distance D>0 with ρ=D/2 violates the stated bound.

failure_location.quote: we have that $W_t\lesssim t^{2n-1}$ as $t\to\infty$. Therefore, we have $\delta_t\lesssim1/t$ as $t\to\infty$, so $\ell(\gamma_t)\asymp t^{2n}$ and $\varepsilon_t\asymp t^{2n}/t^{2n+1}=1/t$ as $t\to\infty$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either weaken the statement to ε_t≲1/t, or add the short density argument for W_t≳t^{2n−1}; replace the W_t bound by W_t≤4(|Y_t|−1)ρ_t justified via the bottleneck property of minimum spanning trees.
issues.overall_effect: The two-sided asymptotic ε_t≍1/t in thm:main (and thm:even) is only half proved; the constant in the W_t bound is incorrect.
issues.title: Proof of Theorem thm:main establishes only ε_t≲1/t and asserts an unjustified MST bound
issues.why_classification: The meaningful direction (ε_t→0 at rate 1/t) is established; the missing lower bound and constant are routine local additions.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the set $\{(0,0,1),(0,0,-1)\}$, the curve $s\mapsto(\cos s,\sin s,0)$, and the balancing constant $1/3$ constitutes a hybrid 3-design

issues.failure_explanation: Hybrid designs use uniform weight ρ/|X| on the set. Splitting off the circle S^d∩P from γ transfers total weight (1−ρ)·|S^d∩P|/ℓ(γ) (not 2π/ℓ(γ) unless the circle is great) to the s points X_P, and merging with X into one uniformly weighted set requires ρ/|X|=(1−ρ)|S^d∩P|/(s·ℓ(γ)). Counterexample to the stated 'iff': octahedron vertices with empty curve and ρ'=1 is a hybrid 3-design; the remark with ℓ(γ)=2π gives ρ=1−1=0, but ({±e_3}, equator, 0) is not a hybrid 3-design (the equator is not a 3-design curve); the correct constant is 1/3 as the paper itself states. For Ehler's tetrahedral example (non-great circle) the formula even gives ρ<0.

failure_location.quote: $(X,\gamma,\rho)$ is a hybrid $t$-design if and only if $(X\cup X_P,\gamma_P,\rho+2\pi/\ell(\gamma))$ is a hybrid $t$-design.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate with ρ'=ρ+(1−ρ)|S^d∩P|/ℓ(γ) under the compatibility condition ρ/|X|=(1−ρ)|S^d∩P|/(s ℓ(γ)) (or use non-uniform weights).
issues.overall_effect: Remark rmk:hybrid is false as stated; the concrete hybrid examples following it remain correct by direct computation.
issues.title: Hybrid-design exchange remark has wrong balancing constant and omits weight compatibility
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the formula and an explicit compatibility hypothesis restore a comparable remark; no dependents are lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we take $X_0$ to be the union of the vertices of a regular $(t+1)$-gon on each element of $Y_{y_0}:=Y\setminus\{y_0\}$

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims |X_0|≍t^{d−1} with d=2n+1. But X_0 consists of (t+1)(|Y|−1) points with |Y|≍t^{2n}, so |X_0|≍t^{2n+1}=t^d, not t^{d−1}.

failure_location.quote: whose constituent point sets and curves have asymptotic orders of size and length $t^{d-1}$ and $1$ respectively

issues.overall_effect: The stated asymptotic for the hybrid construction's point sets is incorrect; nothing else depends on it.
issues.title: Wrong asymptotic order for the size of the hybrid-design point sets
issues.why_classification: Single incorrect exponent in a side remark with an immediate correction.
